main_text.head: PRÆLECTIO PRIMA. IN Qua proponitur & explicatur Con-scientiæ Definitio.
I COR. II. 11.

p.i: Quis hominum novit quæ sunt hominis, nisi Spiritus hominis qui est in ipso?

main_text.p: PErmagnam esse {*} vim Conscientiæ in Cic. pro Milone utramque (fiduciæ metúsque) partem & prudentes viri olim docuerunt, & satis attestatur proprius cujusque sensus & experientia. Quò magis dolendum est, plerosque mortalium, dum rerum mediocriter utilium Scientiam anxiè venantur, in tam crassa interim conscientiæ suæ ignorationc versari. Quâ tamen non est alius quisquam, aut monitor fidelior, aut accusator diligentior, aut testis gravior, aut judex incorruptior, aut solator jucundior, aut hostis importunior. Ut itaque decantatum illud jam olim γνῶθι σεαυτόν[?] studiosorum auribus & mentibus instillarem, ipsóque ab inanis scientiæ nimiâ cupiditate modicè diverterem, & ad majorem Conscientiæ curam cultúmque sensim invitarem; existimavi operæ me facturum pretium, si in Conscientiæ

page.notes: Page number read as "1" from a decorative numeral at top right; please confirm. The mark after "esse" is a small raised sign, transcribed as "*"; the note on the right carries the same mark. "ignorationc" is printed that way and is left as printed. The Greek "σεαυτόν" is uncertain and marked [?]. The verse reference "II. 11." is copied as it appears in the scan. Long s is normalised to plain s (eft → est, fiducia → fiduciæ, atteftatur → attestatur, hoftis → hostis). The page is the start of a division, so there is no running head. Show-through text at the top and the neighbouring page's edge at the left are excluded.
